title: One field label repeated for a public key and a secret key in one input
summary: One input holds the same field label twice (key in two array objects, a repeated STRIPE_KEY line, key under two different parents) with a documented publishable value in one place and a documented secret value in the other; the order is swapped in one fixture and the carrier changed in another, with identical value bytes.
rationale: Where the label repeats, the label cannot tell the two values apart, so the distinction must come from each value's own documented grammar. A recogniser that decides per label, or per input, reports both values or neither; the expected span covers the secret value only. This guards attribution inside a single input and is distinct from the single-value label-conflict cases.

expectation.rationale: Flagged, with one span on the secret value and none on the publishable one. Each provider documents the secret type as not safe to expose and the publishable type as safe to expose; the two classes are told apart by the documented prefix, not by the shared label. Silence on the publishable value follows from the documented class and is stated here as inference.

sources.supports: Key types table: a secret API key (sk_...) is 'Safe to expose: No' and has unrestricted permissions on all Stripe APIs; 'Only publishable keys are safe to expose outside your application's backend.'

Key types table: a publishable API key (pk_...) is 'Safe to expose: Yes' and can be included in front-end code or distributed applications; it cannot perform sensitive operations such as creating charges or reading account data.
